    n = instance['n']

    k = instance['k']

    # edge cases handled by brute force anyway
    for r in range(0, min(k, n) + 1):

endpoint in ``C``) and also dominates its own leaf (the leaf is adjacent to the
vertex itself).  Hence ``C`` is a dominating set of size ``≤ k`` in ``G'``.

original vertex must belong to ``D`` (otherwise the leaf would be undominated).

all edge‑vertices, which means it hits at least one endpoint of every original
edge – i.e. it is a vertex cover of size ``≤ k``.

building ``G'``.  If the original graph has no edges we output an empty graph,
which is a trivial yes instance for both problems.

    Also returns a mapping from old vertex indices to new contiguous indices.

        used.add(v)
